title: Inference runway health & fiscal action plan
summary: Quarterly health check focused on usage patterns, an unexpected cost spike in December, options for reducing unit cost (batching/quantization/dedicated pool), and a 3-month pilot SOW for reserved capacity. Customer wants security pack + SOC2 artifacts and a perf bench across peak traffic windows.
topics: Dedicated vs hosted routing for peak hours
Batching and KV cache impact on p99 latency
next_steps: Yael to send tailored pilot pricing and 3 capacity scenarios (by 2027-01-28)
Priya to schedule perf benchmark with Sapphire traffic replay (aim for week of 2027-02-07)
Redwood to share SOC2 report, SAML SSO guide, and KMS integration notes (by 2027-01-29)
Customer to confirm internal stakeholders and sign-off timeline (Liam/Maya by 2027-01-31)
action_items: Yael Cohen | Prepare pilot pricing: 3 tiers (burst, reserved, hybrid) and expected unit cost delta | 2027-01-28
Priya Nair | Run perf benchmark with sample traffic (10k reqs ramp, 99th percentile target) and share results | 2027-02-09

transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-01-25 15:00 PST
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Yael (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Maya (Sapphire Head of ML), Tom (Infra), Liam (PM)

Summary (auto): Quick recap of last quarter, focused on a December cost surge tied to a model rollout, discuss mitigations (batching/quantization/dedicated nodes) and next-step pilot with security paperwork.

[00:00] Yael: Hi everyone thanks for joining, we'll do a 45 minute checkpoint, quick health read then action items. How's everyone?
[00:12] Maya: Hey Yael, doing well. We saw a big bump in December — that was the main reason for this check-in.
[00:20] Yael: Yeah we flagged that — Priya did some initial telemetry. Priya do you want to run through what we saw?
[00:28] Priya: Sure, um so looking at the traces dec 18-30 there was a 2.8x token increase, but also the average seq length went up from 160 to about 540 chars, sorry tokens, and a lot of the requests hit the long-context model variant. The net effect was both higher tokens and more KV cache misses so CPU + GPU time per request jumped.
[00:50] Tom: We also had a couple of retry storms from the client side during Black Friday, which exacerbated the traffic. Some of those retries were due to our temporary routing change.
[01:02] Maya: Right and our cost went up ~360% month over month on the inference bill part — we want to avoid that.
[01:10] Yael: Understandable. There are three levers we typically recommend: 1) model routing rules — route to smaller variants for non-critical flows, 2) caching/prefix reuse and batch sizing to amortize per-token overhead, 3) reserved/dedicated capacity for predictable throughput.
[01:28] Liam: Can you quantify how much reserved capacity would save? Our CFO wants numbers.
[01:34] Priya: Ballpark — for sustained baseline traffic a reserved GPU pool reduces unit cost by 20-35% based on current profiles; hybrid bursts still using hosted for top 5% peaks. We'll send modeled scenarios.
[01:46] Yael: We'll put together three scenarios in the sheet — burst-only, reserved baseline + burst, and full reserved. We'll include estimated amortized per-1k-token cost and p99 latency expectations.
[01:58] Tom: We're also worried about private deploy constraints — our security team requires VPC private endpoints and HSM-backed KMS for keys. Is that supported in Redwood Private?
[02:10] Priya: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed VPC peering and KMS/HSM integrations, though there are network windows for peering. We'll include the security pack and the SAML SSO guide.
[02:22] Maya: We need SOC2 artifacts, data retention policy, and audit log formats.
[02:28] Yael: We'll share the SOC2 report and the audit-log export schema. Expect separate doc links in the follow-up.

[02:40] (short pause, background typing)

[02:55] Priya: On the perf side — for the bench we'd like a sample week of traffic, ideally replayed with same seq length distribution. For caching to be representative send us prompt families so prefix/KV behavior is realistic.
[03:10] Maya: We'll pull a scrubbed sample and token histogram by tomorrow.
[03:16] Liam: One question — how does quantization affect our quality for the long-context customer support model? We can't accept >2% drop in accuracy for intents.
[03:26] Priya: Good callout. Quantization (8-bit/4-bit) can reduce cost significantly but quality impact varies. For some models 4-bit introduces small regressions on certain classification tasks; we recommend running A/B with the same eval prompt set. Redwood Optimize can suggest quant/profiles by workload.
[03:46] Maya: We definitely want that A/B test; can Redwood host the eval or do we run locally?
[03:52] Yael: We can host or provide a reproducible harness. For pilot speed we usually host a controlled A/B with telemetry captured — quicker for iterate.

[04:05] Tom: From infra, we need to know about egress and VPC peering time windows — last time it took two weeks to schedule. Can that be faster?
[04:14] Priya: It can depending on region and your infra calendar. We'll propose a peering window and try to line up with your ops team. We'll also provide a checklist so you can run parallel approvals.
[04:26] (brief crosstalk)
[04:35] Maya: What about SLAs for p99 latency — we're aiming for sub 450ms for the customer-facing flows. Is that realistic on reserved nodes?
[04:44] Priya: For sub-500ms it's feasible with right instance types and batching limits; we need traffic profile to size. The p99 is trickier under sudden bursts; dedicated with autoscale warm pools helps.
[04:56] Liam: Are there tradeoffs between batching and latency for small requests? Our chat widget includes a lot of short-turn exchanges.
[05:03] Priya: Yes batching increases throughput but for single-shot short messages it can add 20-80ms depending on batch window. We recommend adaptive batching (short window micro-batches for chat, longer windows for background generation). Redwood supports per-route batch configs.
[05:20] Yael: For the pilot we'll recommend per-route configs: chat route: micro-batch 20ms, background generation: 100-200ms window and KV cache warmup.

[05:32] (unintelligible / overlap)
[05:45] Tom: On the cost sheet, will you break out GPU amortization vs token compute vs network egress? Our finance needs that granularity.
[05:53] Yael: Yes the pricing sheet will include token compute, storage/KV, GPU runtime, and egress — and an assumed 3% network overhead we observed.
[06:03] Maya: One of our concerns is regression during model upgrades; how do rollouts work? We need canary and automatic fallback to last stable for any regressions.
[06:12] Priya: Redwood supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies tied to quality metrics and latency. You can pin a version per route and configure auto-fallback thresholds.
[06:24] Liam: Great. What is the simplest way to start the pilot? We want minimal infra lift.
[06:30] Yael: Typical path: 1) sign pilot SOW (3 months), 2) share scrubbed traffic and grant a staging API key, 3) Redwood runs perf bench and suggests config, 4) agree on reserved capacity and start canary. We can spin up a temporary dedicated pool for the pilot if you want isolation.
[06:48] Maya: That sounds good. CFO will want to see the three scenarios.
[06:52] Yael: We'll prioritize the pricing sheet and security docs in the follow-up. Priya will own the perf bench.

[07:00] (swap to wrap-up)
[07:05] Yael: Quick recap of action items: Yael send pricing, Priya schedule bench, Maya to send samples, Tom to check peering windows, customer to confirm sign-off timeline. Any other items?
[07:18] Liam: Can you include an estimate for 99.9th percentile cost impact if we keep the long-context model for top-10% traffic? CFO likes worst-case scenarios.
[07:26] Priya: We'll add a 99.9th percentile stress column in the sheet.
[07:32] Maya: Thanks everyone — let's reconvene after the bench results.
[07:36] Yael: Thanks all, we'll follow up with docs and the spreadsheet by Friday.

(End of recording)
